title: Two Microscopic Mechanisms of Piezomagnetism in CoF$_2$ from First-Principles Calculations
authors: Hiroshi Katsumoto, Tamio Oguchi, Kunihiko Yamauchi
abstract: Rutile-structured CoF$_2$ has long been recognized as a prototypical piezomagnetic material. Recently, it has attracted renewed interest as an altermagnet, exhibiting spin-split electronic bands even in the absence of spin-orbit coupling. Although the piezomagnetic response of CoF$_2$ has been extensively discussed from the viewpoint of magnetic symmetry, its microscopic origin has remained elusive. First-principles calculations reveal two distinct microscopic mechanisms of piezomagnetism in CoF$_2$. Under $xy$ shear strain, the local volumes of the CoF$_6$ octahedra surrounding the two Co sites become different, leading to unequal magnetic moments on the two sublattices and hence a net magnetization. In contrast, under $yz$ shear strain, the piezomagnetic response originates from spin canting induced by the Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya interaction through spin-orbit coupling. The presence of two distinct microscopic mechanisms may be a general feature of piezomagnetic antiferromagnets.
summary: This theoretical study uses first-principles calculations to uncover the microscopic origins of piezomagnetism in $	ext{CoF}_2$. It reveals two distinct mechanisms: strain-induced moment imbalance via octahedral volume changes under $	ext{xy}$ shear, and spin canting driven by the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction under $	ext{yz}$ shear. This suggests that piezomagnetism in antiferromagnets can arise from fundamentally different physical origins.
main_problem: To reveal the microscopic origins of piezomagnetism in the prototypical piezomagnetic and altermagnetic material, $	ext{CoF}_2$.
main_result: Two distinct mechanisms were found: one nonrelativistic mechanism driven by unequal local volumes under $	ext{xy}$ shear strain, and a relativistic mechanism arising from $	ext{SOC}$-induced spin canting via the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction under $	ext{yz}$ shear strain.
method: First-principles electronic-structure calculations using DFT with the PAW method, incorporating noncollinear formalism and applying specific shear strains ($	ext{xy}$ and $	ext{yz}$).
model_or_system: The study focuses on the rutile-structured $	ext{CoF}_2$ crystal, analyzing its magnetic and electronic response when subjected to external shear strains.
key_observables: Induced magnetization ($M$), local volumes of $	ext{CoF}_6$ octahedra, local magnetic moments on different sublattices, and piezomagnetic tensor components ($\Lambda_{ijk}$).
important_parameters: Shear strains ($\varepsilon_{	ext{xy}}, \varepsilon_{	ext{yz}}$), the presence/absence of Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC), and doping levels (pristine vs. hole-doped).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linear fits for calculating strain-form coefficients within specified strain limits ($|\varepsilon_{	ext{xy}}| \le 0.5$, $|\varepsilon_{	ext{yz}}| \le 1.0$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate structural changes, induced magnetization vs. strain for both shear types, and electronic band structures/PDOS changes corresponding to the different physical mechanisms.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the piezomagnetic response under two distinct shear strains ($	ext{xy}$ and $	ext{yz}$), detailing the physical origin (volume mismatch vs. DMI/SOC) and quantifying the resulting magnetic moments and coefficients.
why_interesting: The identification of distinct, symmetry-breaking mechanisms (one electronic/structural, one relativistic/spin-texture) provides a deep, microscopic understanding of magnetoelectric coupling in transition metal compounds, which is relevant to emergent quantum phenomena.
